metaDescription: Six portable washers, twin tub and fully automatic, compared on load size, spin performance, drainage and setup for apartments, RVs and small spaces.
expertTake: The COMFEE 1.6 cu ft fully automatic is the best overall pick because it needs no manual transfer and offers six programs. The Auertech twin tub is the value pick for owners who accept manual washing. Anyone with a full-size hookup and room should skip portable washers and buy a standard machine.
introParagraphs: A portable washing machine is a compact washer that rolls on casters or sits on a counter, connects to a faucet and drains into a sink or tub. It exists for apartments without hookups, RVs, dorm rooms and tiny homes where a full-size washer is impossible.

The category splits into two designs. Twin tubs wash in one tub and spin in another, needing you to move clothes by hand, while fully automatic portables handle the whole cycle in one drum. The right choice depends on how much manual work you accept, how much water you can drain and how big a load you wash.

products.name: COMFEE 1.6 Cu Ft 11 lb Fully Automatic Portable Washer

specList.label: Programs
specList.value: Normal, quick, heavy, bulk and more

products.description:
The COMFEE 1.6 cu ft handles a full wash, rinse and spin without moving clothes between tubs, which is the main reason it leads this guide. Six programs include normal, quick and heavy settings, so you can match cycle length to load type. An 11 pound capacity covers a few days of laundry for one or two people.

The tradeoff is size and setup. A fully automatic portable needs a faucet adapter and a drain location, and it is larger and heavier than a twin tub. Compared with the 0.9 cu ft COMFEE it offers a bigger drum and more cycle options, and compared with the ROVSUN 25 lb it is smaller but easier to place.

Ownership is simple: wipe the drum and lid after use, leave the lid open to dry and clean the lint filter regularly. Check hoses for leaks every season because a loose clamp is the most common failure. Because it is the model most buyers will pick, it also benefits from a larger body of owner experience, which suggests that the most frequent complaints are about drain hose placement rather than motor failure, so route the hose upward only as far as the manual allows and keep it free of kinks.
products.bestFor: Apartments and small homes that want a hands-off automatic washer.
pros: Fully automatic wash, rinse and spin
cons: Needs a faucet adapter and drain

products.name: ROVSUN 25 lb 2.3 Cu Ft Fully Automatic Portable Washer
products.description:
The ROVSUN is the biggest fully automatic portable washer in this lineup, with a 2.3 cu ft stainless steel drum and a 25 pound capacity. A stainless drum resists staining and odor better than a plastic one, and a capacity near 25 pounds handles bedding and towels that smaller machines refuse.

The tradeoff is bulk. It needs more floor space, a larger drain and a bigger water supply than the COMFEE 1.6. Compared with the Winado 15.6 lb it offers far more capacity, but it is heavy to move.

Keep the lid open after use, clean the filter and check hose clamps. Do not overload it, because an unbalanced load walks across the floor. With a drum this large, mix large and small items so the load balances, and pre-soak heavy work clothes instead of relying on one long cycle. Because it holds more water per cycle than the smaller machines, make sure the drain you choose can accept the flow without backing up.
products.bestFor: Families that need large loads without a hookup.

products.name: Winado 15.6 lb Fully Automatic Portable Washer With Drain Pump
products.description:
The Winado offers a 15.6 pound capacity and a built-in drain pump, which lets it empty into a sink or tub that sits higher than the machine. For apartments and RVs where the drain is awkward, that pump is the most useful feature.

The tradeoff is the usual one for a mid-size portable: it is more capable than the COMFEE 0.9 but not as large as the ROVSUN. Compared with the COMFEE 1.6 it offers a bigger load and a pump but fewer program choices.

Check the pump filter regularly for lint and coins. Run an empty hot cycle occasionally to clear buildup. A pump that moves water upward can also draw lint and small items into the filter housing, so make a habit of checking pockets before loading and of opening the pump filter every month or two, before a blockage turns into a standing pool of water in the tub.
products.bestFor: Small spaces with awkward drain locations.

products.name: COMFEE 0.9 Cu Ft Portable Washer LED Display 5 Cycles
products.description:
The COMFEE 0.9 is the smallest fully automatic washer here, with five programs, three water levels and an LED display. It is designed for a closet or a corner of a small bathroom, where space is the limit.

The tradeoff is capacity. A 0.9 cu ft drum washes a small load and cannot handle bulky bedding. Compared with the COMFEE 1.6 it saves floor space but forces more cycles.

Wipe the drum after use and leave the lid open. Clean the lint filter regularly. Because a small drum fills with very little water, detergent concentration is high, so use less than the label suggests or the clothes will come out stiff and the drum will develop a film that traps odor over the following weeks.
products.bestFor: One person in a very small space.
cons: More cycles for the same laundry

products.name: Auertech 28 lb Twin Tub Portable Washing Machine With Drain Pump
products.description:
The Auertech twin tub has two separate tubs, one for washing and one for spinning, which lets you wash one load while spinning another. A 28 pound combined capacity makes it efficient for large families who accept manual transfer.

The tradeoff is manual work. You move clothes from the wash tub to the spin tub yourself, and you manage water fill and drain. Against the fully automatic COMFEE it costs less and runs faster per load but demands attention.

Rinse the tubs after use and check the drain hose for kinks. Do not overload the spin tub. The spin tub lid has a safety switch that stops the spinner when opened, so never defeat it, and let the tub coast to a halt before reaching in, because a spinning basket can injure fingers even though it looks small and harmless.
products.bestFor: Large loads for people who accept manual transfer.
pros: Wash and spin at the same time

products.name: COSTWAY 12 lb Wash 8 lb Spin Twin Tub Portable Washer
products.description:
The COSTWAY twin tub offers a 12 pound wash tub and an 8 pound spin tub, a smaller and lighter design than the Auertech. It suits one or two people and fits in a closet or RV.

The tradeoff is the same as other twin tubs: manual transfer and attention. Against the Auertech it is smaller and easier to store.

Wipe the tubs after use and keep the lint filter clean. The lighter body is a real advantage for a renter who moves often, and the small spin tub encourages the good habit of spinning delicate and heavy items in separate batches, which reduces tangling and lets the spinner stay balanced. The spin tub is smaller than the wash tub, so do not move more than 8 pounds.
products.bestFor: Small households that accept a twin tub.
pros: Wash and spin at the same time

buyingCriteria.explanation: A twin tub like the Auertech or COSTWAY washes in one tub and spins in the other, and you move clothes by hand. A fully automatic portable like the COMFEE or ROVSUN does the whole cycle in one drum. Twin tubs are faster for several loads and cost less, while automatics save effort. Choose by how much manual work you will accept every week. Twin tub owners usually settle into a rhythm: load the wash tub, set the timer, spin the previous load and hang clothes while the next one washes. That rhythm makes a twin tub very productive, but it only works if you are home. If laundry day means leaving the house, an automatic is the only design that finishes without you, and it is worth the higher price and the extra weight.

A 0.9 cu ft drum handles a small load, a 1.6 cu ft drum about 11 pounds and a 2.3 cu ft drum about 25 pounds. Capacity claims are for dry clothes loaded loosely, so assume real loads are smaller. Bedding and towels need the larger models. A king duvet or a pile of wet towels will exceed the rating of a compact drum quickly, so if you wash bulky items even once a month, size up rather than hoping the cycle will cope. Overloading also raises noise and vibration, leaves detergent in the fabric and wears the motor, which is how a cheap machine becomes a short-lived one.

Portable washers connect to a faucet with an adapter and drain into a sink or tub. A built-in drain pump, as on the Winado and Auertech, lets the machine drain upward. Check your faucet thread type, because many kitchen and bathroom faucets need an adapter. Faucets with a pull-out spray head, an aerator that does not unscrew or a recessed spout may not accept the hose at all, and a leaky connection can pour water onto the floor of a rental. Test the fit with the supplied adapter before the first load and keep a small towel under the connection during the first few cycles.

A better spin leaves clothes less wet and speeds drying. Twin tubs spin in a dedicated tub and usually extract more water than automatic portables. If you air dry indoors, spin matters more than wash speed. In a small apartment, clothes that come out nearly dripping will take a day to dry and may smell musty, while clothes that come out damp will dry on a rack within hours. For that reason many apartment owners treat the spin result as the deciding spec, and some pair a portable washer with a separate small spinner for the final extraction.

Portable washers range from about 20 to over 50 pounds empty. Casters help but a full tub is heavy. Measure the closet or corner and the path to the sink. Remember to leave a few inches around the machine for hoses and ventilation, and check that the floor is level and solid, since a washer on a soft floor will vibrate loudly during the spin phase. A small anti-vibration mat is a cheap fix and often cuts the noise that neighbors complain about.

The COMFEE 1.6 lists six programs while the COMFEE 0.9 lists five programs with an LED display. More cycles help with delicates and heavy soil, but simple controls are easier to use in an RV or dorm. Water level selection matters in places where water is limited, because a smaller fill uses fewer gallons per cycle, and a soak program helps with stained work clothes without running several cycles back to back. Look for an audible end-of-cycle signal if you will be working in another room.

howWeEvaluated.title: Load capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared drum size and rated pounds. Machines with stronger capacity ranked higher. Claims are treated as dry-load ratings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at automatic versus twin tub operation and the number of programs. Fully automatic machines scored higher. Manual transfer was a drawback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked drain pumps and connection details. Machines with drain pumps scored higher for flexibility. Faucet adapters were noted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Space and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared footprints and weights from the listings. Compact machines scored higher for tight spaces. Heavy units lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered hoses, filters and leaks from owner feedback patterns. Simple machines scored better on durability.

cards.label: Twin tub
cards.text: The Auertech and COSTWAY wash and spin at the same time and cost less, but you move clothes by hand.

cards.label: Fully automatic
cards.text: The COMFEE, Winado and ROVSUN run the whole cycle in one drum. They cost more and are heavier, but need no attention.

howToChoose.note: Choose a twin tub for cost and speed, and fully automatic for convenience.

howToChoose.subheading: For RV and Apartment Use Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a small footprint, a drain pump, low water use and casters. Check your faucet thread and drain location before buying.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Winado 15.6 and COMFEE 0.9 are the best match for RVs and apartments. The Auertech is a larger alternative if you accept manual transfer.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you wash weekly for a family, where the ROVSUN or COMFEE 1.6 saves time. A drain pump also earns its cost in awkward spaces.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you wash small loads occasionally. A twin tub like the COSTWAY is enough.

maintenance.why: Moisture breeds mildew and odor. Leave the lid open to dry.
A clogged filter slows drainage and leaves lint on clothes.
Loose clamps cause leaks. Tighten or replace them.
It clears detergent buildup and odor.
Coins and lint block pumps. Clear them before they fail.

faq.q: Do portable washers need a hookup?
faq.a: They need a faucet connection and a drain. Most come with an adapter for standard faucets. Check your faucet thread before buying, and if you rent, confirm that the landlord allows a washer connection and that the drain you plan to use is a proper sink or tub rather than a decorative basin.
Automatic units range from 11 to 25 pounds, twin tubs up to 28 pounds combined. Capacity is a dry-load rating.

faq.q: Is a twin tub worth the effort?
faq.a: If you wash often or in large loads, yes. The time saved is real. If you want to walk away, buy an automatic.

faq.q: Can I use them in an RV?
faq.a: Yes, if you have a water supply and a drain. Check weight and gray tank capacity. Compact models fit best.

faq.q: Why does it walk across the floor?
faq.a: Unbalanced loads cause it. Redistribute clothes and avoid overloading. Place it on a level surface.
Wipe the drum, leave the lid open and run an occasional hot cycle. Use the right detergent amount.
